hero.headline: Debuilding the global music economy.
hero.subhead: The infrastructure behind music royalties hasn't changed since before streaming existed. Collection societies, label back offices and paper contracts still run the money that's owed to the people who made it. Debaser AI joins all the dots for a new generation of catalogue owners.
hero.note: Built for the owners and operators of the asset class.

problem.headline: A trillion-dollar industry, still running on decades-old plumbing.

items.title: Collection societies were built for radio, not streaming.
items.description: CMOs across dozens of territories still reconcile usage with rules and reporting formats designed long before a stream existed. Claims can sit in queues for years.

items.title: Label back offices run on ledgers, not logic.
items.description: Statements, splits and recoupment schedules live in systems patched for forty years, held together by people who remember why.

items.title: Contracts are still paper, functionally.
items.description: Rates, territories and deductions sit in a PDF no machine has read. Every re-key is a chance for money to quietly end up somewhere it shouldn't.

items.title: Metadata was never built for this much scale.
items.description: A missing ISRC or a mismatched title still routes real money into the wrong hands, or nowhere at all, across a catalogue that's supposed to be an asset.

items.title: No single party owns the whole picture.
items.description: Every intermediary was built for their own slice of the process. Nobody sees it end to end, so nobody's been in a position to rebuild it — and the artist waiting on the other end just has to trust the queue.

problem.closingLine: None of this is a scandal. It's just infrastructure nobody's rebuilt since the industry was analogue — and somewhere at the end of it, an artist is still waiting on a statement that doesn't add up.

productFlow.headline: From decades of plumbing to a straight answer.
productFlow.subhead: Debaser doesn't patch the old system. It gives modern catalogue owners a layer built for how music rights actually move today, and how the artists behind them actually get paid.

steps.label: Ingest
steps.description: Statements, contracts and catalogue data, in whatever decades-old format they still arrive in.

steps.label: Match
steps.description: Every payment linked to the ISRC, work, writer and split it actually belongs to, not the one a spreadsheet guessed.
steps.detail: ISRC · ISWC · Work codes · Party IDs

steps.label: Investigate
steps.description: Anomalies, missing income and contract conflicts surfaced before they quietly become somebody else's margin.

steps.label: Explain
steps.description: Every answer traced back to the row, the clause or the file. Not a black box.
steps.detail: Source rows · Contract clauses · Audit trail

steps.label: Resolve
steps.description: Every issue becomes a claim, an approval or an export, before the old system has finished reconciling last quarter.

agents.headline: AI built for the parts of the industry that never got modernised.

items.name: Ingestion Agent
items.description: Reads whatever format decades of legacy systems still export, and maps it into one clean schema.

items.name: Contract Agent
items.description: Reads the contract nobody digitised: rates, splits, territories, recoupment... the lot.

items.name: Matching Agent
items.description: Matches income to the right ISRC, work, writer and recording, across a catalogue nobody fully mapped.

items.name: Exception Agent
items.description: Catches the duplicate, the missing split, the income that quietly disappeared into someone else's process.

items.name: Audit Agent
items.description: Checks what you expected against what actually landed, territory by territory, and builds the case for what's missing.

items.name: Ops Agent
items.description: Turns a royalty run into a queue your team can actually clear, not another spreadsheet to inherit.

agents.note: Every agent works from the same rights graph — the record the rest of the industry never built.

missingMoney.headline: Find the money the old system was never built to find.
missingMoney.subhead: Debaser compares what your catalogue should be earning against what forty-year-old infrastructure actually delivered, and shows you exactly where it broke down.

Missing territories, flagged before a CMO admits it

missingMoney.ctaLabel: See what the old rails are missing

explainability.headline: Every number should be able to defend itself.
explainability.body1: Ask why a number changed, and Debaser traces the answer back to the row, the metadata, the clause, not a collection society's version of events.
explainability.body2: Not a summary. Not a guess dressed up as an answer. A structured explanation with the evidence attached, so your team can check it, not just trust it.
explainability.chatUserMessage: Why did this artist earn less this quarter?
explainability.chatAiResponse: Spotify UK income dropped 31% versus Q1. Two tracks were unmatched due to missing ISRCs, accounting for roughly £3,100 in unattributed income. The producer deduction was also applied before the recoupment threshold, which conflicts with clause 4.2(b) of the recording agreement.

trust.headline: Built for data the old system was never careful with.
trust.subhead: Royalty data is some of the most commercially sensitive information in music. Decades of spreadsheets and portals were never built to protect it properly. We were.

items.title: Role-based access
items.description: Control exactly who sees what; by catalogue, territory, deal type or run stage.

items.title: Audit trails
items.description: Every action is logged with a timestamp and a name. Every output traces back to its source.

items.title: Every answer, sourced
items.description: Nothing ships without evidence. Every answer points back to the row, document or clause it came from.

items.title: Human approval workflows
items.description: Software flags and investigates. A human reviews and approves. No royalty run goes out without sign-off.

items.title: Private workspaces
items.description: Your data stays yours. Isolated tenancy, no cross-client data access by design.

items.title: Exportable evidence
items.description: Every claim and discrepancy exports in a format your legal and finance teams can actually use.

items.title: Designed for compliance
items.description: Built to the governance standards serious music companies already expect.

items.title: Transparent outputs
items.description: Every recommendation comes with its confidence level, its reasoning, and the raw source behind it.

vision.headline: Debase, debuild, defrag, democratise.
vision.body1: A century of ceremony... debased. We see a world where a single graph connects every song, recording, release, contract, owner, use and payment, everywhere, for every revenue stream.
vision.body2: We're starting on the operational layer, where statements pile up, income goes missing, and teams are buried in work that shouldn't need a human at all.
vision.graphCaption: Songs → Recordings → Contracts → Income → Ownership → Usage

earlyAccess.headline: Too much money moves through here to run it on infrastructure this old.
earlyAccess.body: We're working with a small group of labels, publishers and catalogue owners who are done waiting for the old system to modernise itself. If you're acquiring, managing or defending a catalogue because you actually care what happens to the songs in it, not just the spreadsheet, talk to us.

valueProps.text: You'll work with us directly while we build this, not a support queue inherited from someone else's system.

valueProps.title: Shape what we build

valueProps.title: Founding customer terms
